questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini a npe ilana ninu eyi ti ohun kọnsonanti kan ba yipada lati baamu pẹlu ohun ti n bọ leyin rẹ, gẹgẹ bi imu ti n di /m/ ṣaaju /b/ tabi /p/?
questions.explanation: Assimilation (idọgba ohun) is the process by which a sound changes to become more similar to a neighbouring sound, as when a nasal becomes homorganic with the following consonant.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini a npe ohun imu ti o le duro nikan gẹgẹ bi alusilo kan ninu ede Yoruba, bi ninu 'n lọ'?
questions.explanation: A syllabic nasal is a nasal consonant, such as 'n' in 'n lọ' (is going), that functions as a full syllable on its own without an accompanying vowel.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Ninu eto ohun Yoruba, kini a npe iṣẹlẹ ninu eyi ti ohun oke n dinku diẹ sii ju bi o ti ṣe deede nigba ti o ba tẹle ohun isale (downstep)?
questions.explanation: Downstep is a tonal phenomenon in which a high tone is realised at a lower pitch than a preceding high tone, typically triggered by an intervening low tone, without being marked as a full low tone.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini a npe apapọ afoniwasi meji ti a n pe gẹgẹ bi ohun kan laarin alusilo kan naa, bi ninu oro 'túulu'?
questions.explanation: A diphthong is a single syllabic sound formed by the combination of two adjacent vowel qualities pronounced within one syllable glide.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kọnsonanti melo ni a maa n ka si i ninu alfabeti Yoruba boṣewa, ti a ba ka awọn to didapọ (digraphs) gẹgẹ bi ẹyọkan?
questions.explanation: Standard Yoruba orthography is generally described as having eighteen consonant letters/sounds (including digraphs like gb, ṣ, and the nasal-marked letters), distinct from the seven oral vowels.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini a npe ilana ninu eyi ti afoniwasi kan n ni ipa lori afoniwasi miran laarin oro kan naa lati je ki won baamu ni ipo bi ẹnu n ṣe si i (vowel harmony)?
questions.explanation: Vowel harmony describes a pattern in which vowels within a word tend to share certain articulatory features, such as advanced or retracted tongue root, influencing how following vowels are pronounced.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini a npe ohun /w/ ati /y/ ninu ede Yoruba, ti won n ṣiṣẹ bi afara laarin afoniwasi ati kọnsonanti?
questions.explanation: Glides (semi-vowels) such as /w/ and /y/ share properties of both vowels and consonants, often functioning as a transitional sound between a consonant and a following vowel.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Ninu ọrọ ' found ehingbe' (bi a se n pe oro Yoruba kan pẹlu ohun imu ṣaaju kọnsonanti bii /b/), kini idi ti /n/ fi n di /m/ ni ilana isọ oro?
options: Nitori idọgba ohun pẹlu ipo enu ti kọnsonanti to tele e
Nitori ami ohun n fẹ ki a ṣe bẹẹ
Nitori a fẹ yi itumọ oro naa pada
Nitori ko si idi fonẹtiki kankan
questions.explanation: A nasal typically assimilates to the place of articulation of a following consonant (e.g. becoming bilabial /m/ before a bilabial stop like /b/ or /p/), a purely phonetic conditioning, not a semantic one.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini a npe atunkọ oro kan patapata tabi apakan rẹ lati fi han itumọ tuntun tabi lati fun un lokun, gẹgẹ bi 'wewe' lati 'wẹ'?
questions.explanation: Reduplication is a morphophonological process in which part or all of a root is repeated to form a new word, often intensifying meaning or forming derived nominal/adjectival forms.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Ninu itupale ohun ti ede Yoruba, kini a npe ẹsẹ kan ti a n pe ni ohun ti n rọra gòkè lati ipo isale de ipo oke ninu alusilo kan naa (rising glide tone)?
questions.explanation: Beyond the three basic level tones, Yoruba also exhibits gliding (contour) tones, where the pitch rises or falls within a single syllable, often realised on certain vowel sequences.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini a npe ami ti a n lo ṣaaju oro-ise lati fi han pe iṣẹ kan n lọ lọwọ lọwọlọwọ, gẹgẹ bi 'ń' ninu 'Ó ń jẹun'?
options: Ami akoko ti o ti kọja
questions.explanation: The marker 'ń' preceding a verb indicates the progressive aspect, showing that an action is currently ongoing, as in 'Ó ń jẹun' (He/she is eating).

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini a npe oro ti a n lo lati fi kọ iṣe kan silẹ ninu gbolohun Yoruba, bi 'kò' ninu 'Kò lọ sí ọjà'?
questions.explanation: 'Kò' functions as a negation marker in Yoruba, placed before the verb to negate the action, as in 'Kò lọ sí ọjà' (He/she did not go to the market).

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini a npe oro ti a n gbe siwaju gbolohun tabi apa kan gbolohun lati tẹnu mọ ọn, bi 'ni' ninu 'Adé ni ó lọ'?
questions.explanation: 'Ni' functions as a focus marker in Yoruba, drawing emphasis to the element it follows, as in 'Adé ni ó lọ' (It was Adé who went).

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini a npe iru gbolohun ninu eyi ti oro-ise meji tabi ju bẹẹ lọ ba wa ni itẹlera lai ni oro-asopọ laarin won lati fi han iṣẹlẹ kan naa, bi 'Ó mu ọbẹ gé eran'?
questions.explanation: A serial verb construction strings together two or more verbs sharing a subject and describing a single connected event, without an intervening conjunction, a common feature of Yoruba syntax.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini a npe ìṣe ti a n lo aṣokọwe 'a-' lati ṣe oro-oruko lati inu oro-ise, bi 'akọrin' lati 'kọrin'?
questions.explanation: Prefixing 'a-' to a verb root is a common Yoruba word-formation strategy that derives an agentive noun, denoting the doer of the action, as in 'akọrin' (singer) from 'kọrin' (to sing).

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini a npe gbolohun ti n so idi ti nkan kan fi le ṣẹlẹ ti nkan miran ba ti kọkọ ṣẹlẹ, bi 'Bí ó bá rọ̀jò, a kò ní lọ'?
questions.explanation: A conditional sentence expresses that one event or state depends on another, typically introduced by 'bí' (if), as in 'Bí ó bá rọ̀jò, a kò ní lọ' (If it rains, we will not go).

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini a npe oro-ise iranlọwọ ti a n fi kun oro-ise akọkọ lati fi han akoko tabi ipo, bi 'máa' ninu 'Yóò máa lọ'?
questions.explanation: An auxiliary verb supports the main verb to express aspects such as habitual or future continuous action, as in 'máa' combined with a main verb.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini a npe ẹka gbolohun ti n ṣàpèjúwe oro-oruko siwaju sii, ti a n bere pẹlu oro-nfiropo ibatan bi 'tí', bi ninu 'Ọkunrin tí ó wọ aṣọ pupa'?
questions.explanation: A relative clause, introduced in Yoruba by 'tí', provides additional descriptive information about a preceding noun, as in 'Ọkunrin tí ó wọ aṣọ pupa' (The man who wore a red garment).

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini a npe iṣẹ ti a n ṣe lati fi han pe iṣẹ kan ti n lọ lọwọ ni akoko to ti kọja, gẹgẹ bi 'ń' pẹlu 'ti' ninu 'Ó ti ń kọ ẹkọ'?
options: Akoko ti n lọ lọwọ ni ti kọja (past progressive)
questions.explanation: Combining 'ti' with the progressive marker 'ń' before a verb conveys that an action was already ongoing at a past reference point, a past progressive construction.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini a npe ọna ti a n fi ṣe afiwe iye tabi didara nkan meji ninu ede Yoruba, gẹgẹ bi lilo 'ju' ninu 'Ó ga ju ẹgbọn rẹ̀ lọ'?
questions.explanation: Comparative constructions in Yoruba are commonly formed using 'ju...lọ', expressing that one entity exceeds another in a given quality, as in 'Ó ga ju ẹgbọn rẹ̀ lọ' (He/she is taller than his/her elder sibling).

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini a npe oro ti a n lo lati ṣe apejuwe ohun tabi iṣe pẹlu ohun ti n fara wé bi nkan naa ti n dun tabi ri, bi 'gbagada' fun ohun ti n ṣubu wuwo?
questions.explanation: Ideophones are vivid words that evoke sensory impressions such as sound, movement, or manner, widely used in Yoruba to add expressive, descriptive colour to speech.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini a npe ẹya gbolohun ti a n lo lati fi han pe ẹnikan tabi nkan kan n gba iṣe kan laisi so ẹni ti n ṣe iṣe naa, iru si 'passive voice' ni Gẹẹsi?
questions.explanation: Yoruba lacks a direct grammatical passive voice like English, but achieves a similar effect through impersonal constructions (often using 'a' as a generic subject) that background the agent of the action.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini a npe iwe ti a n kọ ni ọna girama ti o ye, ti o ni akọle olugba, ọjọ, ati ọwọ olukọ ni ipari, ti a n fi ranṣẹ si ile-iṣẹ tabi oṣiṣẹ kan?
questions.explanation: A formal/official letter (iwe iṣẹ) follows a structured format with a formal register, addressed to an official recipient, and typically ends with the sender's signature and details.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini iyato akọkọ laarin iwe si ọrẹ (informal letter) ati iwe iṣẹ (formal letter) ninu ede Yoruba?
options: Iwe si ọrẹ n lo ede alaraye ti ko le, iwe iṣẹ si n lo ede to muna ti o tẹle ilana girama pipe
Iwe si ọrẹ gun ju iwe iṣẹ lọ nigbagbogbo
Ko si iyato kankan laarin awọn mejeeji
Iwe iṣẹ ko ni akọle rara
questions.explanation: An informal letter to a friend uses relaxed, familiar language, while a formal letter maintains a strict, polished register appropriate for official or professional correspondence.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini a npe ọrọ ti a n ka niwaju ọpọlọpọ eniyan lati gbe ero kan ga tabi lati kilo fun won nipa nkan kan, gẹgẹ bi ọrọ ààrẹ kan?
questions.explanation: A public speech (ọrọ ẹnu) is a spoken address delivered before an audience, typically aimed at informing, persuading, or motivating listeners on a given subject.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Nigba ti a ba n tumọ owe Yoruba kan si Gẹẹsi, kini o le fa iṣoro julọ ti a ko ba ṣọra?
options: Ko si iṣoro kankan lati ṣe bẹẹ
Isọnu ti itumọ jinlẹ ati aworan ti a fi n gbe ero owe naa jade
Ọrọ owe naa yoo gun ju bi a ti fẹ lọ
Ede Gẹẹsi ko ni oro fun ẹranko rara
questions.explanation: Idiomatic and culturally rich expressions such as proverbs are difficult to translate literally, since a word-for-word rendering often loses the figurative imagery and deeper cultural meaning.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini a npe aroko ti o n fi awọn ero meji lodi si ara won ki a to yan eyi ti o dara ju, gẹgẹ bi 'Ilu ha dara ju abule lọ?'?
questions.explanation: An argumentative or comparative essay weighs two sides of an issue against each other before arriving at a reasoned conclusion, as suggested by a topic framed as a question of preference.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini akọkọ ti a gbọdọ ṣe amojuto nigba ti a n ṣe akopo ìròyìn (report) ninu ede Yoruba lẹhin iṣẹlẹ kan?
options: Ki a fo alaye pataki nipa iṣẹlẹ naa
Ki a fi ododo ati alaye to ye kun akopo naa laisi fi ero ara ẹni kun ọrọ naa
Ki a kọ ìròyìn naa ni ede miran ju Yoruba lọ
Ki a fi ero ara ẹni ṣàkópọ̀ gbogbo alaye naa
questions.explanation: A good report should present facts and relevant details objectively, avoiding the intrusion of the writer's personal opinion into what should be a factual account.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini a npe iru ijiroro ninu eyi ti ẹgbẹ meji n fi ero won lodi si ara won niwaju awọn onidajọ lati jere ariyanjiyan kan?
questions.explanation: A debate (àríyànjiyàn) is a structured contest in which opposing sides present arguments for and against a motion, judged on the strength and persuasiveness of their reasoning.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini idi to ye ki a mọ ipele ìjìnlẹ̀ èdè (register) ti o yẹ ki a lo nigba ti a n kọ iwe tabi aroko ninu ede Yoruba?
options: Nitori ipele ede to yẹ da lori ẹni ti a n ba sọrọ ati idi ti a fi n kọ ọrọ naa
Nitori gbogbo iru iwe ni ede kan naa ni a maa n lo
Nitori ipele ede ko ni ipa lori bi a se n loye ọrọ naa
Nitori Yoruba ko ni ipele ede oriṣiriṣi
questions.explanation: Choosing the appropriate register matters because the level of formality suited to a piece of writing depends on the intended audience and purpose, whether an official letter or a casual note.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini iyato laarin kika-yára (skimming) ati kika-àyẹ̀wò (scanning) gẹgẹ bi ilana kika ninu idanwo Fahimta?
options: Skimming ni a n lo fun ẹsẹ ẹwi nikan
Skimming n wa akopo gbogbogbo ẹsẹ, scanning si n wa alaye kan pato ninu rẹ
Scanning n gba akoko ju skimming lọ nigbagbogbo
Won je ilana kan naa lai si iyato
questions.explanation: Skimming involves reading quickly to grasp the overall gist of a passage, while scanning involves searching rapidly for a specific piece of information within the text.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Ti a ba pade oro ti a ko mọ itumọ rẹ ninu ẹsẹ Fahimta, kini ọna to dara julọ lati mọ itumọ rẹ nibẹ?
options: Lilo itumọ akọkọ ti a ba ti gbọ ri lai wo bi o ṣe baamu
Lilo awọn ami inu gbolohun ti o yi oro naa ka (context clues)
Yiyipada gbogbo ẹsẹ naa si ede miran
questions.explanation: When encountering an unfamiliar word, examining the surrounding words and sentence context provides clues that help deduce the most likely intended meaning within that passage.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini iyato laarin ibeere ti n beere fun koko-ọrọ akọkọ (main idea) ati ibeere ti n beere fun alaye atilẹyin (supporting detail)?
options: Koko-ọrọ akọkọ ko ṣe pataki ninu ẹsẹ kankan
Alaye atilẹyin nikan ni a maa n beere ninu idanwo
Ibeere koko-ọrọ akọkọ n beere fun ero gbogbogbo ẹsẹ, ibeere alaye atilẹyin si n beere fun ẹri kan pato ti n gbe koko-ọrọ naa lárugẹ
questions.explanation: A main-idea question asks for the overall central point of a passage, while a supporting-detail question asks for specific facts or examples that reinforce that central point.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini a n pe agbara lati mọ idi ti onkọwe fi kọ ẹsẹ kan, boya lati kọ ni, lati mu inu dun, tabi lati yi eniyan loju (author's purpose)?
questions.explanation: Identifying the author's purpose involves determining whether the writer's primary aim was to inform, entertain, persuade, or otherwise affect the reader, which shapes how a passage should be interpreted.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini a npe ihuwasi tabi ero inu ọkan onkọwe si koko-ọrọ ti a le mọ lati inu awọn oro ati ara ti won lo ninu ẹsẹ kan (tone)?
questions.explanation: Tone refers to the author's attitude toward the subject matter, conveyed through word choice and style, and can be identified by analysing the diction and mood of the passage.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Nigba ti a ba n ṣe akopo ẹsẹ kan, kini a gbọdọ yẹra fun ki akopo naa le dara?
options: Fifi alaye kekere ti ko ṣe pataki kun akopo naa dipo ki a dojukọ ohun to ṣe pataki julọ
Fifi ero wa nipa ẹsẹ naa han ni kedere
Kika ẹsẹ naa ni kikun ki a to ṣe akopo
Lilo oro tiwa ni akopo naa dipo ki a daakọ ẹsẹ naa gangan
questions.explanation: A good summary should focus on the most essential points of the passage and avoid cluttering it with minor, non-essential details that dilute the central message.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini a npe lilo ede ti ko ni itumọ taara, bi apejuwe tabi afiwe, ti onkọwe fi n gbe ero jinlẹ jade ninu ẹsẹ ẹwi?
questions.explanation: Figurative language and imagery use non-literal expressions such as comparisons and vivid description to evoke deeper meaning or sensory impressions, common in poetic passages.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Ti akẹkọ kan ba n ka ẹsẹ pipẹ kan fun idanwo Fahimta ti akoko rẹ ko pẹ, kini ilana to dara julọ ki o le dahun ibeere daradara?
options: Ki o kọ ẹsẹ tuntun dipo ẹsẹ ti a fun un
Ki o kọkọ ka ibeere naa ki o to ka ẹsẹ naa, ki o le mọ ohun to yẹ ki o wa fun
Ki o fo gbogbo ẹsẹ naa ki o dahun lati inu amoro lasan
Ki o ka ẹsẹ naa ni ẹẹkan lai wo ibeere rara
questions.explanation: Previewing the questions before reading the passage helps a student focus their reading on the specific information needed to answer accurately, an efficient strategy under time pressure.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini a npe akojọpọ owe ti a n lo lati kọ awọn ọmọde iwa rere nipasẹ apeere ti a fi ẹranko ṣe, gẹgẹ bi itan Ijapa?
questions.explanation: Animal folktales, often featuring the trickster tortoise Ijapa, are a form of oral narrative used to teach moral lessons to children through entertaining, symbolic stories.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini ipa ti Ijapa (tortoise) n ṣe ojukokoro ninu ọpọlọpọ itan alọ apamọ Yoruba?
options: Ẹranko akikanju ti ko sise aṣiṣe rara
Ẹranko ọlọgbọn ẹrẹ (trickster) ti ojukokoro rẹ maa n mu u wọ wahala
Ẹranko ti n dari gbogbo awọn ẹranko miran ni alaafia
Ẹranko ti ko fi ọgbọn han rara
questions.explanation: Ijapa (the tortoise) is a classic trickster figure in Yoruba folktales, celebrated for cunning but whose greed or overconfidence frequently leads him into trouble, teaching cautionary lessons.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini a npe iru orin oriki pataki ti a n ka fun ode tabi ọdẹ ni asa Yoruba, ti n yin igboya ati agbara won?
questions.explanation: Ìjálá is a distinctive genre of chanted oral poetry traditionally performed by and for hunters, praising courage, skill, and the deity Ogun associated with hunting and iron.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini a npe iru orin ìyìn ti a n ka fun iyawo ni ọjọ igbeyawo ninu asa Yoruba?
questions.explanation: Rárà Ìyàwó is a chanted praise performance for the bride during traditional Yoruba wedding ceremonies, celebrating her lineage, beauty, and the union taking place.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini a npe ẹsẹ oríkì Ifá to gun ti awọn Babalawo n lo fun asọtẹlẹ, ti o ni ọpọlọpọ itan ati owe ninu rẹ?
questions.explanation: Ẹsẹ Ifá are the extensive corpus of chanted verses used within Ifa divination, each associated with a specific Odù and containing narratives, proverbs, and moral instruction.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini iyato laarin owe ati ọ̀rọ̀ àpọ́nlé (epithet) ninu Litereso Alenu Yoruba?
options: Owe nikan ni a n lo ninu itan-itan
Won je ohun kan naa patapata
Owe je ọgbọn ti a le lo ni ipo pupọ, ọ̀rọ̀ àpọ́nlé si je oruko iyin ti a fi si ẹnikan tabi nkan pato
Ọ̀rọ̀ àpọ́nlé nikan ni a n lo ninu oriki
questions.explanation: A proverb is a general piece of transferable wisdom applicable across many situations, while an epithet is a specific descriptive praise-name attached to a particular person, deity, or thing.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini a npe itan alaye gigun ti a n so ni ẹnu nipa idasile ilu, idile, tabi baba nla kan ninu asa Yoruba (legend)?
questions.explanation: A legend (ìtàn àtẹnudẹ́nu) is a longer orally transmitted narrative recounting the founding of a town, lineage, or the exploits of an ancestral figure, passed down through generations.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini idi to fa ki ọpọlọpọ owe Yoruba lo apeere ẹranko tabi iseda lati fi ọgbọn han, gẹgẹ bi 'Ọmọ ológìní kì í dàgbà ká má mọ pa eku'?
options: Nitori awọn Yoruba atijọ ko ni oye eniyan miran lati fi ṣe apeere
Nitori ẹranko nikan ni owe Yoruba n so nipa rẹ
Nitori apeere ẹranko ati iseda n so ero jinlẹ di irorun lati ranti ati loye
Nitori a fẹ dojukọ imọ-ẹrọ ẹranko
questions.explanation: Using vivid, familiar imagery from animals and nature makes abstract wisdom easier to remember, visualise, and pass down accurately through oral tradition.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini a npe ilana ninu eyi ti a n lo ibeere ati idahun laarin akorin ati ẹgbẹ akọrin lati ṣe orin ibile Yoruba (call-and-response)?
questions.explanation: Call-and-response is a common performance structure in Yoruba oral music and chants, where a lead singer's phrase is answered by a chorus, reinforcing communal participation.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini a npe orin ẹkún ti a n ka nigba isinku lati ṣàpèjúwe ibinujẹ ati lati yin ẹni ti o ku ninu asa Yoruba?
questions.explanation: A dirge (ẹkún ikú) is a mournful chant performed at funerals, expressing grief while also honouring and praising the life and achievements of the deceased.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Ninu itan alọ apamọ, kini a maa n pe ẹkọ ti a n fẹ ki awọn ọmọdé rí kọ ni ipari itan naa?
options: Ọjọ ti a ti kọ itan naa
questions.explanation: Folktales are typically structured to conclude with an explicit or implicit moral lesson, the key teaching point the storyteller wants the audience, especially children, to internalise.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini a npe oriki ti a n ki fun ilu tabi agbegbe kan pato lati fi han itan ati iyi ilu naa?
questions.explanation: Oriki-ilu are praise chants dedicated specifically to a town or community, celebrating its history, founders, and notable attributes distinct from lineage-based oriki-orile.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini a npe alọ ti idahun rẹ n nilo agbọye ede meji tabi ilaluja oro (pun/wordplay) lati yanju?
questions.explanation: Some Yoruba riddles rely specifically on double meanings, puns, or clever wordplay for their solution, testing not just logic but also linguistic dexterity.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini idi ti Ìjálá fi ni ibatan pẹkipẹki pẹlu Ògún ninu asa Yoruba?
options: Nitori Ògún ni orisa awọn ọdẹ ati alagbede, ti Ìjálá n yin fun agbara ati akikanju
Nitori Ìjálá je orin fun igbeyawo nikan
Nitori Ògún ko ni ibatan kankan pẹlu ọdẹ
questions.explanation: Ògún, as the deity of iron, war, and hunting, is closely tied to hunters, and Ìjálá chants traditionally invoke and honour him alongside celebrating the hunters' own valour.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini a npe itan ti a n so lati salaye idi ti nkan kan fi ri bi o ti ri ninu iseda, gẹgẹ bi idi ti ijapa fi ni ikarahun (etiological/origin tale)?
questions.explanation: Etiological (origin) tales are a folktale subtype that explain how or why a particular natural feature or animal characteristic came to be, blending entertainment with explanation.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini agbekalẹ ti o wọpọ ni ibẹrẹ ọpọlọpọ itan alọ apamọ Yoruba lati fi han pe itan naa n bẹrẹ (opening formula)?
questions.explanation: Yoruba folktale performances traditionally begin with a formulaic call from the narrator ('Alo o!') answered by the audience ('Alo!'), signalling the start of the storytelling session.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini a npe oríkì ti a n ki fun orisa kan pato, gẹgẹ bi Ṣàngó tabi Ọya, ti n ṣàpèjúwe agbara ati iwa won?
questions.explanation: Oríkì Òrìṣà are specialised praise chants dedicated to a specific deity, describing that deity's unique powers, attributes, and mythological exploits.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini idi ti alọ (riddle) fi ka si ohun elo ẹkọ ti o wulo fun ọmọde ninu asa Yoruba, ju bi ere idaraya lasan?
options: Ko ni anfani eyikeyi ju idaraya lọ
O n kọ ọmọde ni ede ajeji nikan
O n ṣe idagbasoke agbara ero ero-jinlẹ ati oye ede laarin awọn ọmọde
O n kọ ọmọde ni iṣiro giga nikan
questions.explanation: Beyond entertainment, riddles help sharpen children's reasoning, observation, and linguistic skills, functioning as an informal but effective educational tool in traditional society.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini a npe orin tabi ẹsẹ ti a n ka lati fi ìfẹ́ ẹnikan han fun olólùfẹ́ rẹ ninu Litereso Alenu Yoruba?
questions.explanation: Love chants or poems (ewi ìfẹ́) form a distinct genre of Yoruba oral poetry, expressing romantic affection and admiration for a beloved.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini a npe ihuwasi ti a maa n so mọ Ṣàngó ninu awọn oriki ti a n ki fun un, ti n ṣàfihàn agbara rẹ?
options: Ìbínú líle, agbára ãrá àti mọ̀nàmọ́ná
Ìfẹ́ fún òkun àti odò nìkan
questions.explanation: Oríkì praising Ṣàngó typically emphasise his fierce temper and formidable power over thunder and lightning, hallmarks of his mythological character.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini a npe iṣẹ́ akorin akọkọ ti n dari ijọ ni ijo Egúngún tabi ninu ijo ijálá, ti n bẹrẹ ọrọ akọkọ fun ẹgbẹ lati dahun?
questions.explanation: In call-and-response performances such as Egúngún chants or Ìjálá, a lead chanter (aṣáájú-orin) initiates each line or phrase for the assembled group or chorus to respond to.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini idi ti ọpọlọpọ owe Yoruba fi n gbe itumọ meji jade — itumọ gangan ati itumọ ìjìnlẹ̀ (literal and figurative)?
options: Nitori won n lo apeere gidi lati kọ́ni ẹkọ nipa ipo igbesi aye ti o gbooro ju itumọ gangan lọ
Nitori a fẹ da eniyan loju ni gbogbo igba
Nitori itumọ ìjìnlẹ̀ ko wulo rara
Nitori itumọ gangan nikan ni o ṣe pataki
questions.explanation: Proverbs typically operate on two levels: a literal surface scenario and a broader figurative lesson about life, allowing a concrete image to teach an abstract truth.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini a n pe iṣẹ litereso ti a kọ ni ọna arọ (prose) gigun ti o ni itan pipe pẹlu ohun kikọ pupọ, gẹgẹ bi aramada Yoruba?
questions.explanation: A novel (aramada/aroso) is an extended prose narrative with a full plot and developed characters, one of the major genres within Yoruba written literature.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini a n pe onkọwe olokiki ti a mọ julọ fun aramada 'Ògbójú Ọdẹ Nínú Igbó Irúnmalẹ̀' ninu litereso kiko Yoruba?
questions.explanation: D.O. Fagunwa is widely regarded as a foundational figure in written Yoruba literature, celebrated for pioneering fantastical adventure novels such as 'Ògbójú Ọdẹ Nínú Igbó Irúnmalẹ̀'.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini a n pe eré ti a kọ sile lati ṣe lori itage, ti o ni ipin (acts) ati apá (scenes) ninu rẹ?
questions.explanation: A play (eré oníṣe) is a written literary work intended for stage performance, structured into acts and scenes, distinct from narrative prose like the novel.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini a n pe onkọwe ti a mọ fun ọpọlọpọ eré ati fiimu Yoruba, ti a tun mọ si oṣere ati akewi olokiki (fun apẹẹrẹ eré bii 'Kúrunmí')?
questions.explanation: Adebayo Faleti was a prominent Yoruba writer, poet, actor, and broadcaster, well known for his contributions to Yoruba drama, including works such as 'Kúrunmí'.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini a n pe ẹka ohun kikọ ninu itan tabi eré ti o duro takọtabo pẹlu ẹni akọni (protagonist), ti n mu wahala wa fun un?
questions.explanation: The antagonist is the character or force in direct opposition to the protagonist, driving conflict within the narrative or dramatic plot.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini a n pe ibi ati akoko ti iṣẹlẹ inu itan tabi eré kan ti n ṣẹlẹ (setting)?
questions.explanation: Setting refers to the time and place in which the events of a literary work occur, an important element shaping the mood and context of the narrative.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini a n pe ilana ti onkọwe fi n ṣàkóso bi itan kan ṣe n bẹrẹ, dagba, ati parí (plot structure)?
questions.explanation: Plot structure encompasses the organised sequence of events in a narrative, typically including exposition, rising action, climax, falling action, and resolution.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini a n pe akoonu inu eré tabi itan kan ti o de ipele giga julọ ti ìforígbárí, ki o to bẹrẹ si yanju (climax)?
questions.explanation: The climax is the turning point or peak of tension within a narrative or drama, the moment of greatest conflict before the story begins to move toward resolution.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini a n pe ẹnikan ti n so itan naa fun awọn oluka tabi olugbọ, boya lati oju-iwoye 'emi' tabi 'oun' (narrator)?
questions.explanation: The narrator is the voice that tells the story to the reader or audience, which may adopt a first-person ('emi') or third-person ('oun') point of view.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini a n pe iṣẹ litereso kiko kukuru ti o ni ẹsẹ tí a to sọ ọna, ti n lo ede afiwe ati riru (rhythm) lati fi ero han, ti a kọ sile fun kika tabi kikorin?
questions.explanation: A written poem (ewi kiko) is a shorter literary composition structured with attention to language, imagery, and rhythm, distinct from prose narratives or drama.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Ninu awọn iwe Yoruba ti a n gbaniyanju fun ẹkọ ni ile-iwe girama, kini idi ti a fi n ka Akinwunmi Isola gẹgẹ bi onkọwe pataki?
options: Nitori o kọ iwe imọ-ẹrọ kọmputa lasan
Nitori awọn eré ati aramada rẹ, gẹgẹ bi 'Efunsetan Aniwura', ṣàyẹ̀wò ìtàn àti àsà Yorùbá jinlẹ̀
Nitori o je akewi Gẹẹsi nikan
Nitori ko kọ ohunkohun ninu ede Yoruba rara
questions.explanation: Akinwunmi Isola is a significant Yoruba writer whose plays and novels, such as 'Efunṣetan Aníwúrà', are noted for their deep historical and cultural exploration of Yoruba society.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini a n pe iṣẹ litereso kiko ti onkọwe fi n ṣàpèjúwe igbesi aye ara rẹ gan-an ninu iwe (autobiography)?
questions.explanation: An autobiography is a written literary account in which the author narrates events and experiences from their own real life, distinct from a fictional novel.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini a npe igbagbọ ibile Yoruba pe eniyan le tun bi wa si aye leyin iku won, paapa gẹgẹ bi ọmọ inu idile kan naa (reincarnation)?
questions.explanation: Àtúnwáyé is the traditional Yoruba belief that a deceased ancestor's spirit can return to be reborn, often within the same family lineage, distinct from other spirit phenomena like àkúdàáyà.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini a n pe ẹya ara ọ̀rọ̀ àkóso ayé ẹmi ti a gbagbọ pe ẹnikan yan kadara ara rẹ ṣaaju ki o to wa si aye, ninu igbagbọ ibile Yoruba?
questions.explanation: Orí, in traditional Yoruba cosmology, is believed to be the spiritual essence chosen by an individual before birth that determines their destiny and fortune in life.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini a n pe ẹgbẹ́ àṣírí (secret society) ibile Yoruba ti n ṣe idajọ ati atilẹyin fun oye ninu diẹ ninu awọn ilu Yoruba atijọ?
questions.explanation: The Ògbóni society is a traditional Yoruba secret institution historically involved in governance, judicial matters, and supporting the installation and accountability of traditional rulers.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini a npe irubo tabi ijọsin ti awọn ọmọ ilu n ṣe fun awọn baba nla won ti won gbagbọ pe won pada wa si aye gẹgẹ bi ẹmi, pẹlu ijo eegun ninu asa Yoruba?
questions.explanation: The Egúngún masquerade cult centres on ancestral veneration, with masked performers believed to embody the spirits of departed ancestors returning to interact with the living community.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini a npe igbagbọ ibile Yoruba nipa ọmọ ìbejì (twins), pe won ni agbara pataki ti o yatọ si awọn ọmọ miran?
questions.explanation: Yoruba tradition holds twins (ìbejì) in special spiritual regard, believed to possess unique powers and requiring particular rites and reverence, including the carving of ère ìbejì figures if a twin dies.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini a n pe agbara ẹ̀mí burúkú ti a gbagbọ pe awọn obinrin kan (paapaa) ni, ti won le lo lati pa eniyan lara laisi lilo ohun elo gidi, ninu igbagbọ ibile Yoruba?
questions.explanation: Àjẹ́ refers to the traditional Yoruba belief in witchcraft, a spiritual power believed to be wielded, often secretly, to cause harm to others without physical means.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini a n pe orisa ti a gbagbọ pe o da eniyan ni apẹrẹ lati amọ̀ ni ile-iṣẹ ọrun, ki Olodumare to fi ẹmi sinu wọn?
questions.explanation: Ọbàtálá, also known as Òrìṣà-Ńlá, is traditionally credited in Yoruba belief with moulding the physical form of human beings from clay before Olódùmarè breathes life into them.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini a n pe orisa omi tútù (odò) ti a gbagbọ pe o ni ibatan pẹkipẹki pẹlu iya ati abo ninu igbagbọ ibile Yoruba, yato si Ọ̀ṣun?
questions.explanation: Yemọja is traditionally revered as a maternal river/ocean deity closely associated with motherhood and fertility, distinct from Ọ̀ṣun who is specifically linked to the Osun River.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini ipa Ẹ̀ṣù n ṣe ninu igbagbọ ibile Yoruba, gẹgẹ bi a se n loye rẹ ninu ẹsin Ifá?
options: Onibarasọrọ ati alaṣẹ ẹnu-ọna laarin ọrun ati aye, ti n gbe ẹbọ dé ọ̀dọ̀ àwọn òrìṣà
questions.explanation: Ẹ̀ṣù is understood in Ifá belief as a divine messenger and gatekeeper who mediates between the spirit world and humanity, delivering sacrifices to the other deities.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini iyato akọkọ laarin igbagbọ nipa Emèrè ati Àkúdàáyà ninu asa Yoruba ibile?
options: Won je ohun kan naa gan-an
Àkúdàáyà nikan ni o ni ibatan pẹlu ọmọde
Emèrè n tọka si orisa kan, kii ṣe eniyan
Emèrè n tọka si ọmọ ti o ni asopọ pẹlu aiye ẹmi lati ibimọ, Àkúdàáyà si n tọka si ẹni ti o ti ku ti n farahan bi eniyan alaaye
questions.explanation: Emèrè describes a child spiritually linked to the spirit world from birth, while àkúdàáyà refers to a deceased person believed to reappear and live again among the living, two distinct spirit-related concepts.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini idi ti Ifá ṣe pataki to gẹgẹ bi ọ̀nà àsọtẹ́lẹ̀ ninu igbesi aye ojoojumọ awọn Yoruba ibile, ju bi ẹ̀sìn lasan?
options: Ko ni ipa kankan lori ipinnu ojoojumọ
O n dojukọ iṣowo okeere nikan
O n rọpo gbogbo iru oogun ibile
O n ran awọn eniyan lọwọ lati mọ ipinnu ti o dara julọ ninu ọrọ igbesi aye, ilera, ati ayanmọ won
questions.explanation: Beyond being a religious system, Ifá divination has traditionally served as a practical guide helping individuals make informed decisions about major life matters, health, and destiny.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini a n pe ilana ti a gbagbọ pe o le yi ipa-ọna kadara buburu kan pada nipasẹ ẹbọ ati irubo ti Babalawo ba daba, ninu igbagbọ ibile Yoruba?
questions.explanation: Making a prescribed sacrificial offering (ẹbọ) is a central practice in traditional Yoruba belief, understood as a means of averting misfortune or securing favourable outcomes as revealed through divination.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini a n pe irubo ti a n ṣe ni ọjọ keje tabi ọjọ kẹsan lẹhin ibimọ ọmọ lati fun un ni oruko ninu asa Yoruba?
questions.explanation: Ìsọmọlórúkọ is the traditional Yoruba naming ceremony, typically held about a week after a child's birth, during which the child is formally given names before family and community.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini a n pe akojọ ohun ti a n lo ni ibile ninu irubo igbeyawo Yoruba, ti o ni obì, ọti, ati owó ninu rẹ, ti idile ọkọ n mu wa fun idile iyawo (bride price items)?
questions.explanation: Traditional Yoruba marriage rites include the presentation of a customary list of items (bride-price items), such as kola nuts, drinks, and money, from the groom's family to the bride's family.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini a n pe eto awujọ ibile ti n pin awọn ọmọkunrin sinu ẹgbẹ gẹgẹ bi ọjọ-ori won lati ṣe iṣẹ agbegbe pọ, gẹgẹ bi ẹgbẹ Ẹgbẹ́?
questions.explanation: The age-grade system traditionally organised young men (and sometimes women) into cohorts by age, who performed communal labour and social duties together within the community.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini a n pe ipo aṣaaju ti o wa labẹ Oba ninu ilana isakoso ibile diẹ ninu awọn ilu Yoruba, ti n dari agbegbe kekere kan?
questions.explanation: A Baálẹ̀ is a traditional community or quarter head who administers a smaller settlement or section of a town, typically under the overall authority of the reigning Oba.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini a n pe àjọyọ̀ ọdọọdún olokiki ni ilu Òsogbo ti n bọlá fun Òrìṣà Ọ̀ṣun, ti o n fa arinrin-ajo lati gbogbo agbaye wa?
questions.explanation: The Osun-Osogbo Festival is a major annual traditional festival held in Osogbo honouring the river goddess Ọ̀ṣun, renowned internationally and recognised by UNESCO.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini a n pe eto ninu eyi ti ọdọmọkunrin kan n gbe pẹlu ọga-iṣẹ kan fun ọpọlọpọ ọdun lati kọ́ iṣẹ ọwọ kan gẹgẹ bi alagbede tabi aṣọ híhun (apprenticeship)?
questions.explanation: Apprenticeship (ìkọ́ṣẹ́) is a traditional system in which a young person lives and trains under a skilled master craftsperson over an extended period to learn a trade.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini a n pe eniyan ti iṣẹ rẹ ni lati kede iroyin pataki fun gbogbo ilu ni ibile, nigbagbogbo pẹlu ohun elo bi agogo tabi ilu?
questions.explanation: A town crier traditionally served the important role of publicly announcing news, decrees, or events to the wider community, often using a bell or drum to gather attention.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini idi to fi je ki Ẹgbẹ́ Ògbóni ṣe pataki ninu ìṣàkóso ìbílẹ̀ diẹ ninu awọn ilu Yoruba, ju bi ẹgbẹ́ àṣírí lasan?
options: Won n dojukọ ere idaraya lasan
Won ko ni ipa kankan ninu isakoso ilu
Won maa n kopa ninu idajọ, imọran fun Oba, ati ìdánimọ̀ oye titun
Won n dojukọ iṣowo ọjà nikan
questions.explanation: Beyond secrecy, the Ògbóni society traditionally played a substantive governance role, involved in judicial matters, advising the Oba, and legitimising chieftaincy appointments in some Yoruba towns.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Bawo ni a se ka nọmba 'mẹẹdogun' (15) ninu ede Yoruba?
questions.explanation: 'Mẹẹdógún' is the Yoruba word for fifteen, formed on the vigesimal base pattern (literally 'five short of twenty').

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Bawo ni a se ka nọmba 'aadọta' (45) ninu ede Yoruba, ti a mọ pe eto kika Yoruba n lo idinku (subtraction) fun awọn nọmba kan?
questions.explanation: The Yoruba numeral system often uses a subtractive pattern for certain numbers approaching a round base; 45 is expressed as 'aadọta din márùn-ún', literally 'fifty minus five'.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Bawo ni a se ka nọmba 'ọgọ́rùn-ún méjì' (200) ninu ede Yoruba?
questions.explanation: 'Igba' is the distinct traditional Yoruba word for two hundred, illustrating how certain multiples in the vigesimal system have unique standalone names rather than simple compounding.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini a n pe iye Omoluabi ti n fi otitọ ọrọ sisọ ati iwa han ni gbogbo ipo, laisi ẹ̀tàn?
questions.explanation: Truthfulness (òtítọ́) is one of the core values expected of an Ọmọlúàbí, emphasising honesty and integrity in speech and conduct.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini a n pe ọ̀nà ìbọ̀wọ̀ ti a n fi n kí àgbà ọkùnrin nípa dídọ̀bálẹ̀ (prostrating) ninu asa Yoruba?
questions.explanation: Ìdọ̀bálẹ̀ (full prostration) is the traditional gesture of deep respect performed by males when greeting elders or superiors in Yoruba culture, distinct from the kneeling (ìkúnlẹ̀) typically performed by females.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini a n pe ọ̀nà ìbọ̀wọ̀ ti a n fi n kí àgbà obìnrin nípa kíkúnlẹ̀ (kneeling) ninu asa Yoruba?
questions.explanation: Ìkúnlẹ̀ (kneeling) is the customary gesture of respect traditionally performed by females when greeting elders in Yoruba society, paralleling the male gesture of prostration.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini a n pe imọran to wa ninu owe Yoruba 'Ajọbí kìí burú kó tán' nipa iye ìdílé àti ìbáṣepọ̀ ẹ̀jẹ̀?
options: Ẹ̀jẹ̀ ìbátan kò ṣe pàtàkì rárá
Owe yìí ń sọ̀rọ̀ nípa iṣẹ́-àgbẹ̀ nìkan
Ìdílé kò ní ìtumọ̀ kankan mọ́ ní àkókò ìsọ̀de-òní
Ìdílé kìí já pátápátá bí ó ti wù kí ìṣòro tó pọ̀ tó láàrin àwọn ọmọ ìdílé
questions.explanation: This proverb conveys the value that family bonds, however strained, are never entirely severed, reflecting the deep importance placed on kinship (ajọbí) in Yoruba society.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini a n pe iye Omoluabi ti n fi ìtẹríba fún àwọn òfin àti ìlànà àwùjọ hàn, kì í ṣe ìṣọ̀tẹ̀ sí wọn?
questions.explanation: Obedience and respect for established social order (ìgbọràn) is regarded as an important Ọmọlúàbí trait, reflecting cooperation with communal norms and authority.
